questions.question: Is `1.1.0` a real export version or a phantom?
questions.answer: Phantom in practice: the adapter accepts it (server/projects.ts:42) and a test exercises a review-only export, but workflow/export_state.py:19 only writes 1.2.0. Harmless; documents the slice-B-only shape.

questions.question: Are 1.0.0 exports still fully served?
questions.answer: Yes. `review`/`inputs` are optional on a non-strict `z.object` (server/projects.ts:144-170); a 1.0.0 run projects exactly as before, the review node keeps `session_id`/`result_uri` null (test 'legacy' asserts `values.review` is never projected), and the new routes return 404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` / `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`.

questions.question: Can a policy that passed `prepare` be rejected by the adapter's stricter inputs rules?
questions.answer: Not on the rules I checked: workflow/verification.py:50-68 enforces unique check IDs, `safe_path` owned paths and browser⇔scenarios, matching validateRunInputs. The one gap is lane names: the policy schema allows any `node_id` but the adapter only accepts `ui`/`adapter` (server/projects.ts:141).

questions.question: Does the interrupted→paused mapping change existing runs?
questions.answer: No evidence it does: only `review` emits `interrupted` (workflow/automatic.py:314,345); the pre-existing worker interrupt is on node `controller` (automatic.py:512), which `eventNode` ignores. The 'status-bearing events only' change (projects.ts:842) is global but existing `stopped` records sit on nodes that carry evidence.

questions.question: Could `/inputs` leak a path through unredacted receipt fields?
questions.answer: Not from what the controller writes: `launch.status` is one of `launching`/`attached_session_available`/`needs_reconciliation` and `observed_state` is the `claude agents` state (workflow/interactive.py:120,141,143,164,211); the receipt's `error` field is not exported (export_state.py:93-101). `checks[].command`/`setup[].command` are policy-authored and pass through unredacted (projects.ts:441,456).

groups.title: Contract 1.2.0: reviewResult and runInputs payloads
groups.what: Adds `reviewResultSchema` (v1.ts:63-82) and `runInputsSchema`/`runInputWorkerSchema` (v1.ts:86-146) under a new `contract_version: '1.2.0'` literal (v1.ts:7), registers both in `schemas` (v1.ts:153-154), and adds cross-field validators `validateReviewResult` (v1.ts:206-216: approved ⇒ no unresolved P0/P1, diff must be `patch`, no duplicate/quote-less `requirement_found_in`) and `validateRunInputs` (v1.ts:218-232: automatic⇔settings, unique worker/launch/check/scenario IDs, browser⇔scenarios, unconfirmed stop has no time). Existing four payloads keep `1.0.0` (v1.ts:5, README.md:45). Generated JSON schemas and examples are added; the contract test asserts schema/example agreement plus ~28 negative cases (contract.test.ts:59-142).
groups.why: PRD_REVIEW_RESULT §2 (reviewResult 1.1.0) and PRD_RUN_INPUTS §3 (runInputs 1.2.0, requirement links). README.md:43-55 documents the version split and the 404 codes.
groups.how: `z.strictObject` everywhere, so unknown keys are rejected on both sides; `requirement_found_in` is `z.array(z.enum(WORKER_LANES))` with lanes hard-coded to `ui`/`adapter` (v1.ts:50). `diff` reuses workflow-v1 `artifactSchema` (v1.ts:2, 81) so the link is an ordinary artifact reference. `npm run test:contracts` → 13 pass (verified).

groups.title: Adapter: export versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 and strict section schemas
groups.what: `EXPORT_VERSION` literal becomes `EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']` (projects.ts:42, 145). Two strict section schemas mirror `workflow/export_state.py`: `reviewSectionSchema` (projects.ts:73-90, `diff.path` must be the literal `review.diff`) and `inputsSectionSchema` (projects.ts:123-142, `workers` is a `partialRecord` over `ui`/`adapter` with ≥1 entry). Both are `.nullable().optional()` on the export (projects.ts:168-170). A section that fails its schema or cross-field rules makes the whole run `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID` (projects.ts:693-709).
groups.why: README.md:50 and PRD_REVIEW_RESULT §3: old exports serve without the sections; malformed sections are storage errors, never partial payloads.
groups.how: `exportSchema` is a non-strict `z.object`, so a 1.0.0 export (no keys) and an explicit `null` both project to `review: null` / `inputs: null` (projects.ts:694-711) and the new routes answer 404. Test 'exports without a section are served without it' covers 1.0.0, 1.1.0-with-review-only and explicit nulls; the malformed-section test asserts detail, both routes AND the workflow list are 500 (projects.test.ts, cases list incl. `unknown-version: 1.3.0`).

groups.title: Adapter: review projection (redaction, verbatim lane links, diff artifact)
groups.what: `projectReview` (projects.ts:409-422) maps the section onto the contract: `reviewer.session_id`, finding `message` and `requirement` pass through `redactPaths`; `reviewed_at` is normalised to `Z` (projects.ts:371-375); `requirement_found_in` comes from `lanesQuoting` (projects.ts:397-406), which requires the raw quote to be a substring of the raw task (falling back to prompt only when task is empty) AND the redacted quote to survive in the served/bounded text. `diff` becomes a patch artifact `patch-review-<sha256[0:12]>` with a scoped `uri` (projects.ts:366-368, 425-428).
groups.why: PRD_RUN_INPUTS §2: link only on verbatim match, never guess. The bounded-text guard is the audit fix from HANDOFF §6 (quote past the 64K cut must not link) and is asserted in the 'redaction covers paths…' test.
groups.how: Matching against raw text means a quote that names an absolute path still links while its served form shows `<path>` (test 'reviewed', findings[3] vs [4]). Lane selection ignores `finding.worker` entirely: it is every lane whose task contains the quote (test asserts worker `both` → `['adapter']`).

groups.title: Adapter: run inputs projection (bounded text, Z timestamps, receipts)
groups.what: `projectInputs` (projects.ts:431-459) flattens `workers` from a lane-keyed record to an array in export order, sets `launch_node_id = launch_<lane>` when the pinned graph has it else the lane (projects.ts:435), bounds `task`/`prompt` via `boundedText` (projects.ts:378-385: redact first, cut at 65536 UTF-16 units, avoid splitting a surrogate pair, append a counting marker), converts `launch_requested_at`/`stop.confirmed_at` offsets to `Z` and `native_started_at` epoch-ms to ISO (projects.ts:445-446), redacts completion/handoff summaries and drops blank assumptions (projects.ts:449-450). `argv`, `launch_token`, `background_id`, `policy_version` and `failure_drill` are validated but not served.
groups.why: PRD_RUN_INPUTS §4 rules: exact prompt, redaction, bounded reads, pinned per run. Dropping `launch_token`/`background_id` keeps launch secrets and local IDs private (test comment 'tokens and background IDs stay private').
groups.how: Section validation (projects.ts:92-142) is stricter than the policy JSON schema but matches `workflow/verification.py:50-68` (unique check IDs, `safe_path` owned paths, browser⇔scenarios), so a policy that passed `prepare` cannot fail here on those rules. Test 'run inputs are projected in policy order…' pins every conversion including the marker length arithmetic.

groups.title: New routes, store methods and 404 codes; artifact route gains a second registry
groups.what: `RunStore.reviewResult` (projects.ts:592-598) returns 404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` when no section or `attempt !== recorded attempt`; `RunStore.runInputs` (projects.ts:601-605) returns 404 `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`. Routes `/reviews/:attempt` and `/inputs` (projectRoutes.ts:110-111, 167-180) re-run the cross-field validator via `crossChecked` (projectRoutes.ts:71-78 → 500 `RESPONSE_INVALID`) then `conform`. `RunStore.artifact` (projects.ts:613-657) now consults the review-diff registration (`components: ['review.diff']`, projects.ts:616-618) alongside packet artifacts, and refuses content whose byte length differs from the registered size as well as hash mismatches (projects.ts:651-653). The 405/HEAD loop covers the new paths automatically (projectRoutes.ts:113-118).
groups.why: PRD_REVIEW_RESULT §3 adapter deliverables: review route, diff registered as a bounded artifact, legacy runs serve 'no result and no error'.
groups.how: Review diff shares the artifact route's conflict rule: same ID in a packet with a different hash → `EVIDENCE_MISMATCH`. The diff test covers tampered hash, short size, missing file, symlink to outside (refused, content never echoed), over-limit (`ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE`), and `diff: null`. `npx --no-install tsx --test server/projects.test.ts` → 30 pass (verified).
